name: GreeneryIndex
description: Measures overall greenness and livability through vegetation, access, resilience, and connectivity.
what: A composite metric that captures the amount and accessibility of vegetation, connectivity between green spaces, and environmental quality.
why: Helps prioritize areas for greening, measure equity in access to nature, and estimate co-benefits like cooling and pollution reduction.

name: Normalized Difference Vegetation Index
description: The Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) is a metric used to analyze the health and density of vegetation by measuring the difference between near-infrared (NIR) and red light reflectance.
what: A satellite-derived index that quantifies live green vegetation by comparing NIR and red reflectance.
why: Higher NDVI typically indicates healthier, denser vegetation which supports cooling, biodiversity, and stormwater benefits.

name: Tree Canopy Cover
description: Tree canopy cover is the proportion of the ground covered by the vertical projection of a tree's crown and foliage.
what: Percentage of land covered by tree crowns when viewed from above.
why: Canopy provides shade and cooling, improves air quality, and contributes to stormwater interception and habitat.

name: Land Surface Temperature
description: Land surface temperature (LST) is the temperature of the Earth's surface measured from satellites.
what: A satellite-derived measurement of how hot the ground/materials are at the surface.
why: High LST indicates heat-stressed areas that can worsen health risks and energy demand; increasing shade and vegetation can reduce LST.

name: NDVI & LST Time Series
description: Show vegetation health vs. temperature trends over time.
what: A time series chart comparing NDVI and LST across months or years.
why: Shows how vegetation and surface temperatures co-vary, helping assess cooling impacts of greening over time.

name: Tree Canopy % Trend
description: Quick view of canopy gain/loss over time.
what: A chart showing percentage change in canopy cover across years.
why: Identifies areas gaining or losing trees so interventions can target canopy loss or protect gains.

name: Poverty % Comparison vs City Average
what: A comparison of a barangay's poverty rate against the city average.
why: Helps identify socially vulnerable areas where greening interventions should prioritize equity and co-benefits.
